# auto-skeleton API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/documentation.cjs. Do not edit. -->

Geometry-derived loading placeholders over mounted, bounded HTML content.

## AutoSkeleton

Derive Fluent skeleton items from the live geometry of mounted HTML content.
Children stay mounted in a block wrapper. Real text rectangles and visual leaves
produce only circle/rectangle items; text is inset by up to 2px per side for spacing.
Rectangles retain Fluent's rounded corners when content has no measured radius;
positive content radii are preserved and circles use a 50% radius.
Animation defaults to Fluent wave; `animation="none"` uses static themed Fluent items
without shimmer, while preserving loading visibility, focus and aria-busy behavior.
No geometry cache or generated inline styles.
Loading content is hidden/inert only when measurable and native inert is supported.
Otherwise content remains available with aria-busy. Native inert and DOM geometry
are browser requirements; server imports are safe but server rendering has no overlay.
Bounded HTML only: portals, shadow DOM, transforms and nested clipping are unsupported.

### Imports

```ts
import { AutoSkeleton } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import { AutoSkeleton } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/controls';
import { AutoSkeleton } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/controls/auto-skeleton';
```

### Use when

- Representative mounted HTML exists and a loading overlay should follow its measured geometry.

### Avoid when

- Use explicit skeleton placeholders for cold empty data, virtualized content or unsupported transformed geometry.

### Examples

#### Loading a mounted profile

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { AutoSkeleton } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
const isLoading = true;
const photoUrl = '/images/profile.png';
const name = 'Ada';
<AutoSkeleton loading={isLoading} animation="pulse">
  <section><img data-skeleton-shape="circle" src={photoUrl} alt="" /><p>{name}</p></section>
</AutoSkeleton>
```

#### Static placeholders

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { AutoSkeleton } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
const showPlaceholder = true;
function ProfileCard(): React.ReactElement { return <article>Ada — project owner</article>; }
<AutoSkeleton loading={showPlaceholder} animation="none"><ProfileCard /></AutoSkeleton>
```

#### Compose shape container and conditional ignore markers

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Card, CardHeader, Text } from '@fluentui/react-components';
import { AutoSkeleton, useSx, flex, gap } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
function ProfileLoading({ loading, showSummary, ignoreNotes }: { loading: boolean; showSummary: boolean; ignoreNotes: boolean }) {
  const sx = useSx();
  return <div>
    <AutoSkeleton loading={loading}>
      <Card data-skeleton-shape="rectangle"><CardHeader header={<Text>Profile</Text>} /><Text>Profile details</Text></Card>
    </AutoSkeleton>
    <AutoSkeleton loading={loading}>
      <div data-skeleton-container="" className={sx(flex.column, gap.medium)}>
        {showSummary && <p>Profile summary</p>}
        <p data-skeleton-ignore={ignoreNotes ? '' : undefined}>Notes excluded when requested</p>
      </div>
    </AutoSkeleton>
  </div>;
}
```

## AutoSkeletonProps

Props for skeleton geometry derived from mounted, bounded HTML content.
Native div attributes and ref are forwarded to the root. Uses the host Fluent theme
and Griffel renderer; no SPFx provider is required. Native inert and bounded browser DOM
geometry are required for the overlay; server rendering keeps only the content. Apply the content's
flex/grid layout inside children: an owned block wrapper is always present.

### Imports (2)

```ts
import type { AutoSkeletonProps } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
import type { AutoSkeletonProps } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/controls';
import type { AutoSkeletonProps } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit/controls/auto-skeleton';
```

### Examples (2)

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { AutoSkeleton } from '@apvee/spfx-react-toolkit';
const isLoading = true;
function ProfileCard(): React.ReactElement { return <article>Ada — project owner</article>; }
<AutoSkeleton loading={isLoading}><ProfileCard /></AutoSkeleton>
```

### Type

```ts
type AutoSkeletonProps = Omit<React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'div'>,
  'children' | 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML'> & {
  /**
   * Mounted content to measure. Absent/unmeasurable content has no inferred placeholder.
   */
  children: React.ReactNode;
  /**
   * Sets root `aria-busy`. When geometry and native `inert` exist, hides measured content
   * beneath a decorative overlay and releases focus inside it. Otherwise content stays available.
   */
  loading: boolean;
  /**
   * Visual treatment; when omitted, defaults to `wave`. Fluent `wave` and `pulse` respect reduced motion.
   * `none` keeps Fluent items with a uniform themed fill and no animation or shimmer.
   * This affects presentation only: `loading` still controls visibility, inert content and `aria-busy`.
   * @defaultValue 'wave'
   */
  animation?: 'wave' | 'pulse' | 'none';
  /**
   * Minimum normalized width and height in pixels. when omitted, defaults to `8`; nonfinite or nonpositive values throw `RangeError` after mount.
   * @defaultValue 8
   */
  minSize?: number;
  /**
   * CSS selectors excluding matching descendants and their entire subtrees.
   * Malformed selectors throw `SyntaxError` after mount, even when loading is false.
   * The `data-skeleton-ignore` presence marker also excludes a subtree; when omitted, uses no extra selectors.
   */
  ignoreSelectors?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * Direct HTML injection is unsupported; provide rendered children instead.
   * Must be omitted or undefined in this branch.
   */
  dangerouslySetInnerHTML?: never;
}
```
